note: BeyClub's own editorial notes. These are our read on each part, not the Taiwanese or Japanese sources' opinion, and are shown in the app under a 'BeyClub notes' heading. Keyed by 'category:id'. Parts without an entry simply omit the section.

pros: The most successful blade in the tournament record by a wide margin
Outlasts almost anything in a stamina battle once it settles
Flexible — performs on several ratchet and bit combinations rather than one narrow build
cons: Vulnerable to a committed attack type that reaches it early
So common that opponents come prepared for it
blade:UX-03.technique: Launch flat and controlled rather than at maximum power — the goal is a clean, stable spin that survives the opening exchanges, not an aggressive first hit.

pros: Second only to Wizard Rod in recorded placements
Hits hard while still holding a respectable spin
Strong on the widely available 1-60 ratchet
cons: Gives up ground to pure stamina builds if the knockout doesn't land
blade:BX-23.technique: Commit to the attack early. Its win condition is a burst or knockout in the first few exchanges, so launch with pace and angle rather than playing for the long spin.

pros: Consistently one of the highest-placing attack blades
Pairs well with the E bit for an attack build that still finishes spins
cons: Left-spin, so it needs a left-spin launcher
Punished badly by a mistimed launch
blade:BX-34.technique: Left-spin gives it an advantage in opposite-spin matchups — use that deliberately rather than treating it as an ordinary attacker.

pros: Top-tier attack power, rated X by the Taiwanese community
cons: Stamina is its weak point — the source itself flags this
blade:UX-15.technique: Aim to finish the match early. Combine with a ratchet that keeps it aggressive and accept that a long spin is not the plan.

pros: A proven attack blade with a deep tournament record
cons: Loses out to modern stamina blades if the knockout doesn't land
blade:UX-01.technique: A pure aggression pick — launch hard and hunt for the burst.

pros: Balanced enough to handle a range of opponents
Rated highly by both the Taiwanese and Japanese communities
cons: Rarely the outright best answer to any single matchup
blade:UX-08.technique: A dependable all-rounder — a good pick when you don't know what you're facing.

bit:R.technique: Built for rush attacks. Launch with power and aim to end the match in the opening exchanges.
bit:R.summary: An attack bit that moves more predictably than Flat. It performs well in the right build, but it is less adaptable overall.

pros: Low centre of gravity keeps movement steady
bit:LR.technique: A safer rush option than R. Good default when you want attack pressure without throwing away the long game.
bit:LR.summary: A low centre-of-gravity Rush. Sitting closer to the floor makes it more aggressive and gives it real knock-out power — it works well on Impact Drake — but stamina goes quickly.

bit:H.technique: The reliable middle ground — pick it when the matchup is unknown.
bit:H.summary: A hexagonal sole and the UX line's heavyweight defensive option. The polygonal contact gives it a distinctive defensive character with plenty of mass behind it.

pros: The most consistent bit in the game
cons: Needs a strong blade to carry it
Occasionally knocked out by heavy attack
bit:B.technique: Launch for stability. Let the opponent spend their energy attacking and take the spin-finish.
bit:B.summary: A spherical contact point gives the most stable spin support of any bit. It performs on almost any blade, which is why it sits at the top of the meta and in most competitive bags.

pros: A genuine stamina rival to Ball
cons: Its place in the meta is still settling
bit:E.technique: Best on blades that already have the weight to attack — it adds finishing spin rather than raw aggression.
bit:E.summary: A special design that lifts the bey slightly as it spins. Stamina is excellent, making it a real challenger to the Ball family — Whale Wave 5-80E is the build that made its name.

pros: The most successful ratchet in the record
Low profile keeps the bey stable and hard to knock over
cons: Low height gives up some attack angle against taller opponents
ratchet:1-60.technique: The default competitive choice. If you're unsure which ratchet to run, start here.

pros: Nearly matches 1-60 for wins and appears in more distinct combos
Extra contact points help in exchanges
cons: Slightly heavier feel changes launch timing
ratchet:9-60.technique: A strong alternative to 1-60, especially on stamina builds where the extra contact helps survive hits.

pros: Third by wins and one of the most widely played
Good compromise between stability and weight
cons: Outperformed at the very top by 1-60 and 9-60
ratchet:3-60.technique: A solid, forgiving choice while you work out which extreme suits your blade.

pros: Well represented across successful attack builds
Suits blades that want a bit more mass low down
ratchet:5-60.technique: Pair it with attack blades that benefit from the added weight in the exchange.

bit:F.summary: A flat sole meets the floor directly, so friction is high and movement is aggressive. It is the most reliable way to trigger Xtreme Dash, which makes it the usual starting point for attack.
pros: The most consistent Xtreme Dash trigger
cons: Burst of speed fades late in a match

bit:T.summary: A half-flat cone that trades some aggression for stability. Stamina is markedly better than Flat and burst resistance reaches 80, so it suits attack builds that need to survive a long round.

bit:N.summary: A tiny contact point cuts friction and holds the bey spinning in the centre. Centring and stamina are both good; resisting a knock-out is its weak spot.
cons: Sent flying by a committed attack

bit:HN.summary: A taller Needle. The higher centre of gravity adds stability, making it a top pick for defence builds and a frequent sight at tournaments alongside Ball.
cons: Still vulnerable to a clean frontal hit
Depends on blade weight to work

bit:LF.summary: Lower than Flat, so Xtreme Dash triggers constantly and movement is more aggressive. The ceiling is high and the margin for error is not — this is a bit for players who can control it.

bit:O.summary: A larger sphere than Ball, tuned purely towards endurance. In stamina matchups it is a genuine rival to Ball and takes a hit slightly better.
pros: Slightly better knock-out resistance than Ball
cons: Less flexible than Ball across builds

bit:P.summary: An extremely small contact point with almost no friction. Stamina should be excellent in theory, but it wanders off its track when hit, so results are inconsistent.
cons: Squeezed out by Ball and High Needle

bit:S.summary: A fine spike with burst resistance of just 20 — the worst knock-out resistance of any bit. A light touch sends it out of the ring.
cons: The worst knock-out resistance in the game

bit:HT.summary: A taller Taper. The raised centre of gravity shifts its balance point slightly and adds a little stamina, at the cost of steadiness under heavy attack.

bit:GF.summary: A weighted Gear version of Flat with an outer toothed edge for grip. Heavier than Flat and hits harder, which makes it the natural upgrade path for attack.
pros: Heavier and more violent than Flat
cons: Performance drops as the gear wears

bit:GB.summary: A weighted Gear version of Ball. The extra mass improves knock-out resistance while performance stays close to Ball itself.
cons: Slightly less consistent movement than Ball
The added weight wears it faster

bit:GP.summary: A weighted Point. The gear adds mass and improves knock-out resistance, but the Ball family covers the same ground better.
cons: Completely overshadowed by Ball and Gear Ball

bit:GN.summary: A weighted Gear version of Needle, heavier than both Needle and High Needle. The extra mass gives defence builds more presence.
pros: The heaviest of the needle family
Slightly better knock-out resistance than High Needle
cons: Squeezed out competitively by High Needle and Ball

bit:Q.summary: The contact surface produces an irregular, vibrating path that is hard to read. Entertaining, but the outcome leans on luck and stamina drains quickly.

bit:U.summary: A general-purpose balance bit that folds several elements into one sole. It covers attack and defence without being extreme at either.
cons: Falls short on every axis against strong players

bit:C.summary: A spiral sole that produces a distinctive rotating path. It needs the right blade to be worth running; on its own it is unremarkable.

bit:TP.summary: Starts in a Point configuration and changes state when struck. The two-mode idea is interesting, but neither mode is best in class and results are inconsistent.
pros: Two modes give it some adaptability

bit:M.summary: A recent all-round balance bit that combines several performance traits. It arrived late, so competitive opinion is still forming, but early results are solid.
pros: Fits a wide range of builds

bit:A.summary: An active acceleration design whose sole material makes the bey spin faster as the round goes on, triggering Xtreme Dash late. The late-round burst is formidable in skilled hands.

bit:DB.summary: The heaviest bit in the game at about 1.5g, with a wide disc supporting a ball tip and standing nearly 2mm taller than a normal Ball. Tuned well it beats Ball on stamina, but burst resistance of 20 means an upright launch is asking for trouble.
cons: The high centre of gravity demands an angled launch

bit:MN.summary: A metal Needle. Durability and consistency both improve over the plastic version, which is why it has taken over Needle's competitive slot.
pros: Far more durable than plastic Needle
cons: Still carries the needle family's weaknesses
A clean frontal hit can still knock it out

bit:G.summary: A gliding sole whose friction characteristics give it a smooth, distinctive path. A balance pick that covers stamina and defence, with room to surprise in the right build.

bit:FB.summary: A ball tip on a free-spinning mechanism that cuts friction loss, so stamina beats a plain Ball in theory. It is the mechanical upgrade of Ball and Silver Wolf's signature bit.
cons: Performance varies a lot with tuning

bit:L.summary: Designed to keep the bey spinning level throughout the round, and the UX line's stamina flagship. Stamina and stability are both strong; it is Samurai Saber's usual bit.

bit:BS.summary: A spike paired with a bounce mechanism: when struck, the sole pops out and adds stability. A genuinely unusual reactive defence, though its consistency is unproven.
cons: The mechanism does not always trigger

bit:UN.summary: The needle tip sits under the body, dropping the centre of gravity dramatically. That low stance adds stability, and it is Golem Rock's usual partner.

bit:Z.summary: A special sole that produces an irregular, jolting path. Hard to predict and disruptive to an opponent, though not especially stable itself.
cons: A niche position in the meta

bit:J.summary: An impact-focused attack bit, one of the newer UX releases, built to run with Meteor Dragoon. Attack is respectable and its meta standing is still accumulating.

bit:UF.summary: A low variant of Flat that sits closer to the floor and triggers Xtreme Dash reliably. Attack is close to Low Flat but more regular, and it is Shark Scale's partner bit.

bit:V.summary: The CX line's launch bit, with a vortex-shaped sole built to run inside Dran Brave's CX structure. Balanced and a good way into the CX system.
cons: An early CX bit, so not extreme

bit:LO.summary: A low centre-of-gravity CX take on Orb. Steadier than a plain Orb with strong stamina and good knock-out resistance; it shines inside Wizard Arc's CX structure.
pros: Very stable thanks to the low stance

bit:W.summary: A wedge-shaped contact face that supports the bey at an unusual angle. Perseus Dark's dedicated bit, specialised for defence with decent stamina alongside.

bit:K.summary: A pop-out kick mechanism that releases extra attack power when triggered. Inside a CX structure the effect multiplies, which makes it the core of CX attack.
pros: Strong synergy with the CX structure
cons: Burns its own stamina when unstable

bit:GR.summary: A heavier CX version of Rush, with a gear shell and more mass behind every hit. In a CX structure the impact is considerable; it is Fox Brush's configuration bit.
pros: Extra weight means real attack power

bit:Tr.summary: A turbine mechanism that produces a stronger effect the faster it spins. Pegasus Blast's configuration bit — weak early, strong late.
cons: Stamina depends on keeping the revs up

bit:WB.summary: A ball tip with an outer wall structure that adds stability when the wall makes contact. The reinforced knock-out resistance makes it a serious CX stamina-defence option.
cons: Its edge over a plain Ball is inconsistent

bit:TK.summary: Kick and Trans mechanisms combined into a two-mode bit, and Sol Eclipse's configuration. It switches state when struck, which should make it adaptable, though neither mode is top tier.

bit:Op.summary: A complex, actively controlled mechanism and Emperor Might's dedicated bit. The CX synergy is distinctive, but a complicated mechanism means performance falls off noticeably as it wears.
cons: Complexity means wear hurts it badly

bit:I.summary: One of the heaviest attack bits in the CX line, with an ignition design that releases a violent impact on contact. It is Bahamut Blitz's configuration bit and the flagship of CX attack.
pros: The strongest attack bit in the CX line
Heavy, with real impact behind it
cons: Depends heavily on the whole CX build

bit:D.summary: A Basic Line defence bit — a cone tip studded with tiny spheres that lets the bey drift while holding position better than Needle or High Needle.
pros: Better stamina than Needle-family defence bits
Keeps moving instead of locking in place

bit:DS.summary: A reinforced take on Spike — the same sharp tip, but backed by a wider disk that pushes the combo back upright after a hit.
pros: Disk helps recover balance after being knocked off-centre
Some life-after-death from the disk's smooth rim
cons: Still a spike tip underneath — limited stability on its own

bit:FF.summary: Flat's Xtreme Dash specialist. Same flat-with-dimple shape, but the shaft spins free of the ratchet so less stamina bleeds away while dashing.
pros: Free-spinning shaft loses less stamina during Xtreme Dash
Flat contact keeps it aggressive on the rail
cons: Same core limitations as a plain Flat bit otherwise

bit:GU.summary: A Custom Line balance bit — a geared, rounded tip aimed at all-round movement rather than excelling in one stat.
cons: Doesn't lead in any single stat

bit:NR.summary: A compact stamina bit with a reduced 10-tooth gear for controlled, reliable movement on the Xtreme Line — the standout part of its CX-18 release.
pros: Strong stamina despite its small size
Also useful on balance builds for survivability
cons: Fewer gear teeth than Accel-type bits means a slower Xtreme Dash

bit:RA.summary: A rubber-tipped attack bit built for the Xtreme Dash — a wide guard lifts it above the rails, and the rubber gives it real burst resistance at the cost of almost all stamina.
pros: High friction rubber tip gives strong burst resistance
Wide guard helps it ride the Xtreme rail cleanly
cons: Incredibly low stamina from the high-friction tip

bit:WW.summary: Wedge's defence-oriented sibling — the same small sharp tip for stamina, plus a wall rim meant to push the combo upright, but a heavier 16-tooth gear trades some of that stamina for dash speed.
pros: Wall rim aids recovery back to upright
Sharp tip carries real stamina potential
cons: Not a strong pick in a standard defence combo
Considered one of the weaker Custom Line bits by the community

bit:Y.summary: A low-friction stamina bit — a cone-shaped POM tip that trades knock-out resistance and stability for extended spin time.
pros: High stamina from the low-friction POM tip
